take_homes: a spread of views from several agents isn't an answer. Give the synthesizer a frame like diagnosis, policy, actions so it has to choose
split only on access, dialect or stance, otherwise write one prompt
handoffs are where it breaks, e.g. the curator silently dropping a conflict. I should check my own setups for that

monday.move: take one of the engineers' multi-agent setups and add a conflict-log file where the curator has to write down every disagreement between sources instead of picking one silently
monday.who: me, plus one engineer whose pipeline I borrow
monday.when: Tuesday, an hour after standup. Monday is already full
monday.stop_condition: stop if the log is empty after two runs, because then the seam is clean or I'm not catching anything
monday.blocker: the engineers will say their setups are fine, and the org-wide rollout to non-engineers still has no owner for maintenance

misconception.why: I skipped the review step in a couple of places. The synthesis looked good and I couldn't tell whether it was true, and the lecture says the audit checks handoffs, not whether the briefing is correct. 'Good agent means good output' doesn't hold. I wouldn't call it changed, since I'd still skip most checks on routine work.

one_line: the first half repeats what my engineers already do. The 'a framework makes it pick' bit and the part about the curator silently dropping a conflict are worth the day.
